_note: #403. A review is current only while the line it quotes is the reviewed document's one `Version:` line. a-old, b-old and c-old each quote a line that is written in their document and is not its version line: each is stale. b.md and c.md each have two lines starting `Version:`, so nothing says which is the version line: each document is a finding, and c-new, which quotes the newer of c.md's two, is not current either. d-current quotes d.md's one `Version:` line and has no finding: the control. e.md has no `Version:` line, so a review of it is read as before: e-line quotes a line of it and has no finding; e-word quotes a word that is in it and is no whole line, so it is not stale and its Supersedes: line retires nothing; e-older quotes a line that is not in it. #403, review round 1: a document R1 cannot read one version line from is a finding and is never read as having none. Each f- document writes its version line so that it reads as one and does not start with `Version:`, one per kind R1 names: white space, emphasis, a list mark, a quote mark, a heading mark, a backtick, a hidden character, another letter case. Each is a finding and its review, which quotes an older line still written in the document, is not current. g.md has one `Version:` line and the word again in the middle of a prose line: g-current has no finding.
